facts.statement: The genus Martinectes was described by Clark, O'Keefe, and Slack in 2023.
facts.quote: authority: Clark, O'Keefe & Slack, 2023

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Martinectes is Trinacromerum bonneri.
facts.quote: type_species: Trinacromerum bonneri

facts.statement: Martinectes bonneri was previously known as Trinacromerum bonneri and Dolichorhynchops bonneri.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Trinacromerum bonneri Adams, 1997 Dolichorhynchops bonneri (Adams, 1997))

facts.statement: Martinectes lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian stage) in North America and possibly European Russia.
facts.quote: Martinectes is an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian stage) of North America and possibly European Russia.

facts.statement: The genus Martinectes contains only one species, M. bonneri, which is known from multiple skeletons and skulls.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species M. bonneri, known from multiple skeletons and skulls.

facts.statement: Martinectes was a large polycotylid plesiosaur measuring at least around 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a large polycotylid measuring at least around 5 m long.

facts.statement: Two large specimens of Martinectes (KUVP 40001 and 40002) were collected from the Pierre Shale of Wyoming and reported by Adams in her 1997 Masters thesis.
facts.quote: Two very large specimens of a polycotylid plesiosaur (KUVP 40001 and 40002) were collected from the Pierre Shale of Wyoming and later reported on by Adams in her 1997 Masters thesis

facts.statement: In 2023, Clark, O'Keefe, and Slack assigned Dolichorhynchops bonneri from the Sharon Springs Formation to the new genus Martinectes, meaning "Martin's swimmer".
facts.quote: In 2023, Clark, O'Keefe and Slack assigned D. bonneri from the Sharon Springs Formation of the United States to a new genus Martinectes, which means "Martin's swimmer".

facts.statement: In 2025, polycotylid teeth from the Rybushka Formation of European Russia were referred to cf. Martinectes.
facts.quote: In 2025, polycotylid teeth material from the Rybushka Formation of European Russia were referred to cf. Martinectes.

facts.statement: In 2017, Everhart suggested that specimen KUVP 40001 could have measured up to 6 to 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 2017, Everhart suggested that KUVP 40001 would have measured up to 6 - 7 m in length.

facts.statement: In 2025, Zverkov and Meleshin suggested Martinectes was around 5.5 meters long, similar to Polycotylus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Zverkov and Meleshin suggested that Martinectes would have been similar in size to Polycotylus, around 5.5 m long.

facts.statement: In 2026, Zhao estimated Martinectes measured 4.95 meters long and weighed 1.27 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2026, Zhao estimated that Martinectes measured 4.95 m long and weighed 1.27 MT.

facts.statement: Clark, O'Keefe, and Slack (2023) classified Martinectes as a polycotylid member of the clade Leptocleidia, sister to an unnamed polycotyline from the Niobrara Formation.
facts.quote: Clark, O'Keefe & Slack (2023) recovered Martinectes as a polycotylid member of the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia, as the sister taxon to an unnamed polycotyline from the Niobrara Formation.

facts.statement: Martinectes, along with Dolichorhynchops species, forms the clade Dolichorhynchia within the Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: These species, together with Dolichorhynchops spp. (D. osborni and D. herschelensis), form the clade Dolichorhynchia within the Polycotylinae.

facts.statement: Martinectes belongs to the family Polycotylidae.
facts.quote: familia: Polycotylidae

facts.statement: Martinectes belongs to the subfamily Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Polycotylinae

facts.statement: Two large specimens (KUVP 40001 and 40002) were collected from the Pierre Shale of Wyoming and reported by Adams in her 1977 master's thesis.
facts.quote: Dos enormes especímenes de un plesiosaurio policotílido (KUVP 40001 y 40002) fueron recolectados del Esquisto Pierre de Wyoming y más tarde reportados por Adams en su tesis de maestría de 1977.

facts.statement: In 1997, Adams officially described the specimens as a new species of Trinacromerum (T. bonneri).
facts.quote: Más tarde (1997), ella oficialmente los describió como una nueva especie de Trinacromerum (T. bonneri).

facts.statement: In 2008, O'Keefe demonstrated that Trinacromerum bonneri did not belong to Trinacromerum and assigned it to Dolichorhynchops, creating the new combination D. bonneri.
facts.quote: O'Keefe (2008) demostraron que Trinacromerum bonneri no pertenece a Trinacromerum y lo asignaron a Dolichorhynchops, creando la nueva combinación D. bonneri.

facts.statement: Clark et al. found several characters distinguishing D. bonneri from the type species of Dolichorhynchops, establishing the new genus Martinectes for D. bonneri.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Clark et al. (en prensa) encontraron varios caracteres que distinguen a D. bonneri de la especie tipo Dolichorhynchops, erigiendo el nuevo género Martinectes para D. bonneri.

facts.statement: Martinectes lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Martinectes is the clade Dolichorhynchia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dolichorhynchia

facts.statement: Martinectes is classified in the family Polycotylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Polycotylidae

facts.statement: Martinectes is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
